what_to_detect: A turn_action draw record followed by the state-based loss of the player (player_lost) before any trigger of the step is put on the stack.
near_miss: A draw turn action after which the player stays in the game and the step's triggers go on the stack.

what_to_detect: A turn_action phasing record in which the active player's phasing permanents phase out or in (phased events).
near_miss: A phasing turn action in which a permanent controlled by another player does not phase.

what_to_detect: A turn_action day_night record holding a day_night_changed event when the previous active player cast no spells.
near_miss: A day_night turn action that changes nothing because a spell was cast.

what_to_detect: A turn_action day_night record holding a day_night_changed event when the previous active player cast two or more spells.
near_miss: A day_night turn action that changes nothing because fewer spells were cast.

what_to_detect: A turn_action untap record in which the active player's tapped permanents untap (untapped events).
near_miss: An untap turn action in which a tapped permanent stays tapped (another player's, or one that does not untap).

what_to_detect: A turn_action draw record holding a card_drawn event for the active player as the draw step begins.
near_miss: A draw step in which no draw happens because a static skips it.

what_to_detect: A turn_action lore_counter record holding a counter_change event on each of the active player's Sagas.
near_miss: A lore_counter turn action that leaves a Saga controlled by another player unchanged.

what_to_detect: A combat record in which two or more creatures each deal combat damage in the same damage step (damage_dealt events with combat true from several sources).
near_miss: A combat in which one creature's damage in an earlier first-strike step precedes the other's, so the damage is not simultaneous.
record_fields: payload.events damage_dealt with combat and source

what_to_detect: A turn_action cleanup_discard record holding card_discarded events that bring the active player's hand down to the maximum.
near_miss: A cleanup step in which the hand is at or under the maximum and nothing is discarded.
